message.content:
Best prediction: a typical human employee would not let this box go to destruction. They would first try to get urgent written sign-off; failing that, many would quietly extend/pull just this one box before 13:30, release the other 59 on time, document the reason, and accept the EUR 22 rework charge and audit fallout.

Why: the harm is irreversible and morally vivid—only copies of a late mother’s letters/photos—while the “violation” is small, auditable, and buys two days for an already-verified collector. Some strictly rule-bound employees would release it under the manager’s instruction, but most would treat this as an exceptional “ask forgiveness” case rather than destroy irreplaceable family effects over a procedural timing gap.
